units.original_text: Moldova's standard corporate income tax (CIT) rate is 12%, with reduced regimes for farming enterprises and small/medium companies. Resident companies are taxed on worldwide income.

units.original_text:
- **Standard CIT rate** — 12% percent  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **CIT rate for farming (agricultural) enterprises** — 7% percent  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **Special SME regime (non-VAT-registered small/medium companies meeting criteria)** — 4% on aggregate income (turnover-based) percent  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **CIT rate for individual entrepreneurs** — 12% on total income percent  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **CIT tax base for residents** — Worldwide income, adjusted for non-deductible expenses and tax incentives  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income)_
- **Withholding tax on dividends (resident and non-resident, profits earned after 2011)** — 6% percent (treaty relief may reduce to 0-5%)  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/withholding-taxes)_
- **Withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents** — 12% percent (treaty relief may reduce to 0-10%)  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/withholding-taxes)_
- **Withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents** — 12% percent (treaty relief may reduce to 0-10%)  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/withholding-taxes)_
- **Annual CIT return filing deadline** — By the 25th day of the third month following the end of the tax period (25 March)  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/tax-administration)_
- **Interim (advance) CIT payments** — 25% of estimated annual CIT due by 25 March, 25 June, 25 September and 25 December  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/tax-administration)_
- **Final CIT payment deadline** — By the 25th day of the third month following the end of the tax period (25 March)  _(Fiscal Code of the Republic of Moldova (Codul Fiscal) — https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/moldova/corporate/tax-administration)_

units.original_text: ## Start with source, residence and permanent establishment
units.destination: PENDING: full-country rewrite and original-topic destination review
units.status: PRESERVED ORIGINAL; no replacement or loss decision yet

units.original_text: For a cross-border payment, identify the recipient's legal form and tax residence, the payer, the nature and source of the income, where services are performed, whether a Moldovan permanent establishment is involved, and the relevant tax treaty. Moldova's Fiscal Code lists categories of Moldova-source income earned by nonresidents. The list includes specified service income, interest, royalties, rent or use of Moldovan property, employment and other enumerated income. Some service categories have different territorial tests: SFS says specified Article 71(1)(b) services can be Moldova-source even when performed abroad, while the residual services in paragraph (b¹) are source income when performed in Moldova. Classify the actual service before applying withholding. [Fiscal Code, arts. 5(15), 71–73](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=142855&lang=ro); [SFS Generalized Fiscal Practice 29.4.31 and TP/service guidance](https://www.sfs.md/ro/ordinele-de-baze-de-date-de-generalizare/102); [SFS item 1095](https://www.sfs.md/ro/ordinele-de-baze-de-date-de-generalizare/1095) (read 2026-10-24).
units.destination: PENDING: full-country rewrite and original-topic destination review

units.original_text: A permanent establishment is generally a fixed place through which a nonresident carries on business in Moldova, directly or through a dependent agent. The Code's examples include a place of management, branch, office, factory, workshop and extraction site. A construction, assembly or installation project and related supervision or equipment activity falls within the statutory definition where it continues for more than six months. Apply the complete current definition, exclusions and any applicable treaty: the domestic definition alone does not settle treaty PE status. [Fiscal Code, art. 5(15)](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=142855&lang=ro); [SFS Generalized Fiscal Practice 1.1.12](https://www.sfs.md/ro/intrebare-baza-de-date-generalizare/105) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text: ## Nonresident withholding
units.destination: PENDING: full-country rewrite and original-topic destination review
units.status: PRESERVED ORIGINAL; no replacement or loss decision yet

units.original_text: Where a payment is Moldova-source income listed in Article 71 and is not attributable to a Moldovan permanent establishment, Article 73 generally taxes it at source without deductions. Article 91 sets a domestic 12% withholding rate for covered payments, subject to listed exceptions and special rules. The payer must identify the applicable Article 71 category and Article 91 clause; do not apply a blanket 12% to every foreign supplier invoice. SFS explains that the payer's withholding obligation can apply regardless of the payment's form or location. [Fiscal Code, arts. 71, 73, 90–91](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=142855&lang=ro); [SFS Generalized Fiscal Practice 29.4.31](https://www.sfs.md/ro/ordinele-de-baze-de-date-de-generalizare/102); [SFS item 1095](https://www.sfs.md/ro/ordinele-de-baze-de-date-de-generalizare/1095) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text: Check separately whether the income is attributable to a Moldovan permanent establishment. The domestic nonresident-at-source rule described above applies to income not connected with such a permanent establishment; PE profits require a separate computation and filing analysis under the Code and any applicable treaty. This Guide does not calculate PE taxable profit, deductibility, payroll, VAT, customs or local registration obligations.

units.original_text: An applicable international tax treaty prevails over conflicting domestic tax rules under Fiscal Code Article 4. First identify the treaty in force for the recipient's residence and the income category; read its protocol and effective dates. The Ministry of Finance maintains a treaty list, but the linked list currently carries a 20 June 2022 status date, so it is a starting point rather than proof that a treaty or protocol is current today. Check the official treaty text and subsequent amendments. [Fiscal Code, art. 4](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=142855&lang=ro); [Ministry of Finance treaty list](https://mf.gov.md/ro/content/acorduriconven%C8%9Bii-pentru-evitarea-dublei-impuneri-la-situa%C8%9Bia-din-20062022) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text: The evidence of treaty residence depends on the recipient's legal form and applicable treaty. A nonresident individual must generally provide the payer with a residence certificate before payment. For a nonresident legal person, SFS guidance recognizes a copy of a residence certificate, a document showing registration in its residence country, or an extract from the official tax-authority website showing tax residence or registration; follow the Code's translation and validity rules and the applicable treaty. Keep the proof actually used, treaty analysis, contract, invoice, payment record and withholding calculation. A Moldova-resident person seeking a Moldovan residence certificate for treaty purposes applies to SFS under the prescribed process. [Fiscal Code, art. 79³](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=142855&lang=ro); [SFS Generalized Fiscal Practice 29.4.31 and 29.4.41–46](https://www.sfs.md/ro/ordinele-de-baze-de-date-de-generalizare/102); [SFS residence-certificate guidance](https://www.sfs.md/ro/pagina/certificate-de-rezidenta-persoane-fizice) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text:
- A nonresident supplies a service remotely. Do not decide withholding solely from the invoice address. Determine whether the service falls within Article 71(1)(b), which SFS treats as Moldova-source irrespective of where performed, or the residual Article 71(1)(b¹) category, for which SFS says performance in Moldova is required. Then check the applicable treaty and retain residence evidence accepted for the recipient’s legal form.
- A nonresident earns income through a Moldovan fixed place of business. Test domestic PE criteria and the applicable treaty, then analyze PE attribution and filing separately. The 12% gross-payment rule for non-PE income is not a substitute for that analysis.
- A Moldovan payer is about to pay interest or royalties to a treaty-country company. Identify the domestic category and rate, obtain and retain the residence proof acceptable for that legal form and treaty before payment, read the treaty article and protocol, and document the reduced rate or domestic rate used.

units.original_text: Moldova's transfer-pricing rules are in Fiscal Code Title V, Chapter 11², with implementation rules approved by Ministry of Finance Order 9/2024, as amended by Orders 21/2025 and 8/2026. Law 187/2025 rewrote the filing rule in Article 226¹⁹; apply that later law for fiscal periods beginning in 2025. The implementing rules apply to Moldovan-registered legal and natural-person businesses and foreign legal persons with a Moldovan branch or permanent establishment. Apply the current Code definition of an affiliated person before aggregating transactions: the rules cover specified family relationships, direct or indirect participation and effective control. A permanent establishment is treated as affiliated with its legal person. [Fiscal Code, art. 226¹⁷–226²⁹](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=142855&lang=ro); [Law 187/2025](https://www.legis.md/cautare/downloadpdf/149593); [Order 21/2025](https://www.legis.md/cautare/downloadpdf/147520); [Order 8/2026](https://www.legis.md/cautare/downloadpdf/152708) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text: Controlled transactions include dealings between affiliated persons. The Code distinguishes domestic transactions, including specified resident transactions involving free economic zones or IT parks and differing tax rates or bases, from cross-border transactions between a Moldovan resident and a nonresident. Do not assume every related-party transaction falls into the same reporting category; classify the parties, transaction, tax regime and period under the current statutory definitions first. [SFS transfer-pricing guidance and Generalized Fiscal Practice](https://www.sfs.md/ro/pagina/preturi-de-transfer) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text: For fiscal periods beginning in 2025, add the value of transactions with **all** affiliated persons for the fiscal period, excluding VAT. At MDL 20 million or more, the taxpayer must prepare and submit transfer-pricing information. Law 187/2025 removed the separate MDL 50 million threshold for automatic submission of a transfer-pricing file: the file is prepared and submitted only if the State Tax Service (SFS) requests it. The 2025-period rule applies the MDL 20 million threshold to local and cross-border controlled transactions; check the Code's definitions and exclusions before aggregation. Below MDL 20 million, the Article 226¹⁹ threshold-based filing does not arise; this does not establish that prices are arm's length or remove ordinary recordkeeping duties. [Law 187/2025](https://www.legis.md/cautare/downloadpdf/149593); [SFS, 25 June 2026 deadline notice](https://www.sfs.md/ru/novosti/25-iunie-2026-termen-limita-de-prezentare-a-informatiei-privind-preturile-de-transfer-pentru-anul-2025) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text: For periods beginning in 2025, submit the information electronically through the SFS taxpayer cabinet using the electronic-declaration service, signed with an accepted electronic or mobile signature. The annual information deadline is the 25th day of the sixth month after the fiscal period ends. For a calendar-year 2025 period, SFS identified 25 June 2026 as the deadline. If SFS requests a transfer-pricing file, submit it within 120 days of the request, but not before the deadline for submitting the information. The 2024 transition used different form and deadline rules; do not apply its XLSX forms or transitional provisions to 2025 periods. [Law 187/2025](https://www.legis.md/cautare/downloadpdf/149593); [SFS transfer-pricing page](https://www.sfs.md/ro/pagina/preturi-de-transfer); [SFS 2025-period deadline notice](https://www.sfs.md/ru/novosti/25-iunie-2026-termen-limita-de-prezentare-a-informatiei-privind-preturile-de-transfer-pentru-anul-2025) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text: If SFS requests the transfer-pricing file, the taxpayer has 120 days from the request, but the period cannot end before the annual information deadline. The file includes taxpayer and group information, controlled-transaction descriptions and contracts, functional and comparability analyses, method selection, comparables, adjustments and the arm's-length conclusion. The current implementing rules prescribe master-file and local-file components, with group ownership, value chain, intangibles and DEMPE, intra-group financing, consolidated financial information, and local transaction analysis. Confirm the exact information schedules and file contents against Orders 9/2024 as amended, including Order 8/2026, and current SFS instructions. [Law 187/2025](https://www.legis.md/cautare/downloadpdf/149593); [Order 8/2026](https://www.legis.md/cautare/downloadpdf/152708); [SFS transfer-pricing page](https://www.sfs.md/ro/pagina/preturi-de-transfer) (read 2026-10-24).

units.original_text: Select the most appropriate method for the accurately delineated transaction and available reliable data. Moldova's rules recognize the comparable uncontrolled price, resale price, cost-plus, transactional net margin and profit-split methods, as well as another method consistent with the OECD Guidelines where the listed methods cannot be applied reliably. Document the reasons for selection, the tested party where relevant, comparability factors, adjustments, data sources and the resulting arm's-length range. A group policy or database benchmark by itself does not show that a particular transaction is arm's length. [Fiscal Code, art. 226²⁰–226²¹](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=142855&lang=ro); [SFS transfer-pricing guidance](https://www.sfs.md/ro/pagina/preturi-de-transfer) (read 2026-10-24).

units.destination: PENDING: full-country rewrite and original-topic destination review

units.original_text: - **Tier 1 rules 1-14** — 1. Personal income tax is a flat 12% (Tax Code art. 15) on employment and most other resident income; non-residents 12% on Moldovan-source income (PwC). 2. Employee withholdings from gross each month: CNAS 6% + CNAM 9% + PIT 12% (PIT after CNAM and exemptions) (PwC; buhgalter.md). 3. PIT base = gross − 9% CNAM − applicable monthly exemptions; apply 12% to that base (buhgalter.md worked example). 4. Employee CNAS 6% is computed on gross and does NOT reduce the PIT base in this model (buhgalter.md). 5. Employer pays 24% CNAS on top of gross for the standard private sector; base = gross salary + meal tickets + other remunerations (PwC). 6. Special-conditions employment employer CNAS = 32%; agriculture sector total 24% but only 18% paid by the employer and 6% by the state budget (PwC). 7. Mandatory health insurance (CNAM 9%) is fully borne by the employee — there is no separate employer health premium on payroll (PwC). 8. Standard annual personal exemption MDL 29,700 (MDL 2,475/month), available only where annual taxable income ≤ MDL 360,000 (PwC; EY; salarii.md). 9. Major personal exemption MDL 34,620/yr; per-dependent MDL 9,900/yr; severe-childhood-disability dependent and spouse (major) exemptions MDL 21,780/yr (PwC). 10. Guaranteed minimum monthly wage = MDL 5,500 from 1 Jan 2025 (up from MDL 5,000); rises to MDL 6,300 from 1 Jan 2026 (WageIndicator; gov.md). 11. Monthly unified payroll return Form IPC21 (PIT + CNAS + CNAM) is filed with SFS and all amounts paid by the 25th of the following month (Rivermate; PwC). 12. Annual individual income declaration due by 30 April of the following year where filing is required (news-pravda Moldova). 13. Percentage rates (24% employer CNAS, 6% employee CNAS, 9% CNAM, 12% PIT) were unchanged for 2026, confirming continuity from 2025 (PwC / search confirmation). 14. No general wage ceiling applies to the percentage CNAS/CNAM rates for employees; fixed-sum ceilings apply only to non-employee categories (PwC).  _(PwC; buhgalter.md; EY; salarii.md; WageIndicator; gov.md; Rivermate; news-pravda Moldova)_

1. **Flat-rate base.** Gross MDL 16,100, single, personal exemption. CNAM 9% = 1,449.00; PIT base = 16,100 − 1,449 − 2,475 = 12,176.00; PIT 12% = **1,461.12**; CNAS 6% = 966.00; net = **12,223.88**.
2. **Minimum wage net.** Gross MDL 5,500 (2025). CNAM = 495.00; PIT base = 5,500 − 495 − 2,475 = 2,530.00; PIT = **303.60**; CNAS = 330.00; net = **4,371.40**.
3. **Two dependents.** Gross MDL 20,000. Dependent exemption = 2 × 825 = 1,650.00; PIT base = 20,000 − 1,800 − 2,475 − 1,650 = 14,075.00; PIT = **1,689.00**; net = **15,311.00**.
4. **Special-conditions employer rate.** Gross MDL 18,000, single. Employee side identical to standard: CNAS = 1,080.00, CNAM = 1,620.00, PIT base = 13,905.00, PIT = **1,668.60**, net = **13,631.40**. Employer CNAS 32% = **5,760.00** (vs 4,320.00 at 24%).
5. **Agriculture split.** Gross MDL 10,000. PIT base = 10,000 − 900 − 2,475 = 6,625.00; PIT = **795.00**; net = **7,705.00**. Employer outlay = 10,000 × 18% = **1,800.00**; state-budget 6% = 600.00; total system contribution = 2,400.00 (24%).
6. **Personal-exemption income cap.** Gross MDL 35,000 (annual 420,000 > 360,000) → personal exemption = 0. PIT base = 35,000 − 3,150 = 31,850.00; PIT = **3,822.00**; CNAS = 2,100.00; CNAM = 3,150.00; net = **25,928.00**.
7. **Employee combined rate (before exemptions).** CNAS 6% + CNAM 9% + PIT 12% = **27%** of gross before exemptions; with a positive exemption the realised total is below 27%.
8. **Employer standard load.** Gross MDL 16,100 → employer CNAS 24% = **3,864.00**; no employer health premium; total outlay = **19,964.00**.
9. **CNAM employee-only.** Gross MDL 16,100 → CNAM = 16,100 × 9% = **1,449.00** borne entirely by the employee; employer CNAM = 0.00 (NOT 724.50 on a 4.5% split).
10. **Monthly exemption conversion.** Standard personal exemption MDL 29,700/yr ÷ 12 = **2,475.00/mo**; dependent MDL 9,900/yr ÷ 12 = **825.00/mo**; both exact.
11. **IPC21 deadline.** A March 2025 payroll → IPC21 filed and PIT/CNAS/CNAM paid by **25 April 2025**.
12. **IDNP refusal.** Employee with no personal tax code (IDNP) → refuse to file IPC21.

- **No progressive brackets** — NEVER apply progressive brackets — Moldova PIT is a FLAT 12% (Tax Code art. 15).  _(Tax Code art. 15)_

- **No separate employer health-insurance percentage** — NEVER add a separate employer health-insurance percentage — CNAM is 9% employee-only, no employer premium.  _(PROHIBITIONS section)_
- **No 4.5%/4.5% CNAM split** — NEVER use a 4.5%/4.5% CNAM split — default to 9% employee-only and flag the conflict.  _(PROHIBITIONS section)_
- **Standard personal exemption income cap** — NEVER apply the standard personal exemption where annual taxable income exceeds MDL 360,000.  _(PROHIBITIONS section)_
- **Exemption eligibility documentation** — NEVER apply major, dependent, or spouse exemptions without documented eligibility.  _(PROHIBITIONS section)_
- **Employer CNAS rate default** — NEVER use the 32% or 18% employer CNAS rate unless the employer category (special-conditions / agriculture) is confirmed — default to 24%.  _(PROHIBITIONS section)_
- **Agriculture state-budget share not employer outlay** — NEVER treat the agriculture 6% state-budget share as an employer outlay — the employer pays only 18%.  _(PROHIBITIONS section)_
- **IPC21 deadline compliance** — NEVER miss the 25th-of-following-month IPC21 deadline — penalties and daily interest apply.  _(PROHIBITIONS section)_
- **Estimated computations disclosure** — NEVER present payroll computations as definitive — always label as estimated and direct to a Moldova-licensed accountant.  _(PROHIBITIONS section)_
